title: UPAC Work in Progress: Are traversable wormholes physically reasonable?
speaker: Sanne Vergouwen (Utrecht University)
description: UPAC Colloquium (Utrecht Philosophy of Astronomy & Cosmology): work-in-progress session; the draft is sent out beforehand via the upac-l mailing list. Hybrid; the Teams link goes out via the same list.
abstract: Although the Einstein field equations admit solutions with non-simply connected topological configurations such as traversable wormholes, observational evidence of such structures is lacking. A justification of this absence was formulated in 1993 by Friedman, Schleich and Witt in terms of a topological censorship theorem. This theorem states that under certain conditions, there can be no causal curves threading non-simply connected topology. This paper explores the interpretation of this theorem in terms of physical reasonableness. Firstly, I discuss that the topological censorship theorem is naturally interpreted as a no-go theorem stating that traversable wormholes are physically unreasonable. I present several senses in which spacetime models can be considered physically unreasonable, and argue that claims about physical reasonableness should specify which sense is at stake. Secondly, I show that an alternative interpretation of the topological censorship theorem is as providing a no-go result concerning one of the conditions for physical reasonableness used in its derivation, namely the energy condition. I show that the controversy over whether the energy conditions are law-like constraints has consequences for whether traversable wormholes are physically unreasonable in a nomological sense. As such, I argue that progressive development in research on traversable wormholes is driven not by a resolution of what counts as physically unreasonable, but by the persistence of this dispute.
